tryit.text: I have to cut a 50-metre piece of cloth into pieces of 1 metre each. How many cuts will I make at minimum?
tryit.think: Picture cutting a ribbon into 3 pieces at home. How many snips did that take?

tryit.text: Bob's 4 coins are worth 2, 4, 6 and 8. Coin C is worth more than A, and B + C = D. Which two coins can buy a Rs. 14 candy?
tryit.think: Start with B + C = D. Which coin can be the sum of two of the others?

tryit.text: Four buyers come into a chocolate shop one by one. Each buys half of the chocolates left. The fourth buyer buys only 1 chocolate. How many were there at first?
tryit.think: Work one buyer at a time, going backwards: before the 4th buyer there were 2. How many before the 3rd?

tryit.text: Six times me makes a whole and a half. Take me out of a whole and three of me are left. Who am I?
tryit.think: Say it simply: “Six of me make one and a half.”

tryit.text: Prachi is facing North. She takes two right-angle turns in the clockwise direction. Which direction is she facing now?
tryit.think: I know the directions in clockwise order: North, East, South, West.

tryit.text: Which statement is DEFINITELY true about a five-digit number with three odd digits and two even digits?
tryit.think: Ask why sums turn odd or even: odd + odd is even. What do three odd digits add up to?

tryit.text: John has Rs. 12. He buys 3 balls and 2 balloons and has Rs. 2 left, which is the cost of 1 ball. What is the cost of 1 balloon?
tryit.think: Write it as a number sentence: 3 × 2 + 2 × balloon + 2 = 12. Now it is just sums!

backcover_intro: In Class 5, children grow their Computational Thinking skills: reasoning with digits and place value, spotting patterns and breaking a problem into small steps. These are not just computer skills. They are thinking skills for every subject.
